intended_object: An r-uniform hypergraph on vertex type V: a family of r-element subsets of V (the edges). Taken from the docstring and the module documentation, where it is used for edge-density counting in hypergraph regularity.
explanation:
The structure stores a finite set of finite subsets of V and requires every edge to have exactly r elements. This is the usual definition of an r-uniform hypergraph as a subfamily of V^(r), the set of r-element subsets of V.

Mathlib's `Hypergraph` (Mathlib/Combinatorics/Hypergraph/Basic.lean) is set-based. It has no uniformity condition and no finiteness, so it is not the same object. The library provides `toHypergraph` to convert to it. Mathlib's `Set.Sized r` only expresses the uniformity predicate on a family of sets; it is not a hypergraph structure.

Requiring the edge set to be finite is the standard setting for the counting and density theory the module develops. When V is finite, which is the case wherever densities are defined (they need `[Fintype V]`), every r-uniform hypergraph has finitely many edges, so nothing is lost there. The vertex set is the whole type V, which is the usual convention, matching Mathlib's `SimpleGraph`.

The degenerate cases also behave as they should. For r = 0 the only possible edge is ∅. When V has fewer than r elements there are no possible edges at all.
